title: Number of Solutions and Intersections of Trigonometric Graphs: custom lesson practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values, intersection configurations and inequality intervals are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs scope and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: State the number of solutions of the equation $\sin x = 0.8$ in the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
State the number of real solutions of the equation $\cos x = 1.5$ for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$, giving a brief reason.
Find the number of solutions of the equation $\cos(2x) = 0$ in the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
Find the number of points of intersection of the curves $y = \sin x$ and $y = \cos x$ in the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
Find the unique solution of the equation $\sin x = 1$ in the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
State the set of values of $x$ for which $\cos x > 0$ in the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

The function $f$ is defined for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$ by $f(x) = 6 - 4\cos(3x)$. State the number of real solutions of the equation $f(x) = k$ in each of the following cases:
(i) $k = 1$,
(ii) $k = 6$,
(iii) $k = 10$.

The function $f(x) = 5\sin x + 2$ and the line $y = 4.5$ are defined for $0^\circ \le x \le 180^\circ$. The curve and the line intersect at $x = 30^\circ$ and $x = 150^\circ$. State the set of values of $x$ for which $5\sin x + 2 > 4.5$ on the interval $0^\circ \le x \le 180^\circ$.

figure.purpose: Fix the trigonometric graph or triangle configuration for students without revealing the analytical solution.
figure.brief: Draw coordinate axes showing the curve $y = 5\sin x + 2$ and the horizontal line $y = 4.5$ over the domain $0^\circ \le x \le 180^\circ$, intersecting at two points.

questions.prompt: In the diagram, the curve $y = 3\cos(2x) + 2$ and the line $y = 4 - \dfrac{2}{\pi}x$ are drawn for the domain $0 \le x \le \pi$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the endpoints of the line segment on the domain $0 \le x \le \pi$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By considering the values of the curve and the line at key points, determine the number of real solutions of the equation $3\cos(2x) + 2 = 4 - \dfrac{2}{\pi}x$ on the interval $0 \le x \le \pi$, justifying your answer.

questions.prompt: The function $f$ is defined for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$ by $f(x) = 8\sin^2(x) - 3$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State the maximum value and the minimum value of $f(x)$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine the number of solutions of the equation $f(x) = 3$ on the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

figure.purpose: Fix the trigonometric graph or triangle configuration for students without revealing the analytical solution.
figure.brief: Draw coordinate axes showing the trigonometric graph $y = 8\sin^2 x - 3$ over the domain $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

questions.prompt: The equation $3\cos x - \sqrt{3}\sin x = 0$ is defined for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation $3\cos x - \sqrt{3}\sin x = 0$, giving your answers in exact form in terms of $\pi$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: On the same axes, the curves $y = 3\cos x$ and $y = \sqrt{3}\sin x$ are drawn for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$. Find the set of values of $x$ for which $3\cos x > \sqrt{3}\sin x$ on the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

figure.alt_text: Answer-safe graph showing curves y = 3cos(x) and y = sqrt(3)sin(x) on [0, 2pi].

questions.prompt: The curves $C_1$ and $C_2$ have equations $y = 2\sin(2x)$ and $y = \cos x$ respectively, for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Sketch $C_1$ and $C_2$ on the same set of axes for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using your sketch, state the number of points of intersection of $C_1$ and $C_2$ on the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Show that the $x$-coordinates of the points of intersection satisfy $\cos x(4\sin x - 1) = 0$, and hence find all exact solutions of $2\sin(2x) = \cos x$ on $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

questions.prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = 5 - 4\cos^2(2x) + 3\sin(2x)$ for $0 \le x \le \pi$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express $f(x)$ in the form $p\sin^2(2x) + q\sin(2x) + r$, where $p, q, r$ are constants to be found.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By completing the square or otherwise, find the exact maximum and minimum values of $f(x)$ for $0 \le x \le \pi$, and state the range of $f$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt:
State the set of values of the constant $k$ for which the equation $f(x) = k$ has exactly:
(i) $0$ real solutions,
(ii) $4$ real solutions.
